However, a lower A′ leads to reduced heat transfer performance, which can negatively affect charging and discharging rates and round-trip efficiency. This highlights a trade-off: while reducing A′ can lower capital costs, it may compromise system Page 76 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. performance and dispatchability. This trade-off was evaluated through annual technoeconomic simulations. Figure 51b shows how sulfur TES cost scales with increasing storage capacities for a fixed internal TES-HX specific surface area of 2.5 m2/m3. The cost model captures the economies of scale effect, showing a reduction in sulfur TES cost per unit of stored energy as the storage capacity increases. This cost reduction is largely attributed to the decreasing vessel surface area to volume ratio at larger sizes, which lowers the associated material and fabrication cost on a per-kWh basis. It is noted that cost benefit begins to plateau beyond 375 MWh. For A’ of 2.5 m2/m3 and sulfur TES capacity of 475 MWh, the sulfur TES cost is approximately: C = 36 $/kWh.
